brief: Newsquawk previews the US October jobs report (due Nov 6, 13:30GMT/08:30EST). Consensus looks for 63k nonfarm payrolls, up from 29k in September; unemployment is seen holding at 4.2%, though the Chicago Fed's model points to a slight improvement to 4.14%. Average hourly earnings are expected to rise 0.3% M/M and ease to 2.9% Y/Y, which would be the first sub-3% annual print since May 2021. Oxford Economics forecasts a softer 40k print, below consensus but above its own estimated 25k break-even pace, and argues this lets the Fed stay focused on inflation and hike in December; it attributes current price pressure to energy costs and AI-buildout spending rather than wages. Labour proxies mostly ran positive into the survey window: JOLTS openings beat expectations and quits rose sharply, jobless claims stayed low, ADP payrolls beat, and Challenger logged the lowest October job-cut total since 2023, though its hiring-plans jump was driven by seasonal roles. Revelio's data showed slower job growth by contrast. Following the October FOMC, Chair Warsh signalled a measured pace of hikes, and money markets price an 83% chance of a 25bp December hike to 4.00-4.25%.
